item.title: Ukraine Peace Talks Yield Prisoner Deal but No Path to Peace
item.description: The first trilateral negotiations between Russia, Ukraine, and the US since early this year produced a measured humanitarian breakthrough, but little tangible progress toward ending the war. The two days of talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10 -11 reached an agreement in principle on a large-scale prisoner exchange and opened discussions on broader European security arrangements. item.title: Angola Looks to Diversify from Crude with Windfall Oil Revenues
item.description: Angola has accelerated efforts to diversify its economy away from heavy dependence on oil by using this year’s windfall oil revenues to fund reforms and investments in transport corridors, minerals, banking, and tourism industries, according to Citigroup. “We’re definitely seeing a lot of activity and it has the benefit of longer-term political stability, economic stability, which is making it more attractive for foreign direct investment, infrastructure projects, and other longer-term investment,” Citi’s…

item.title: Turkey Agrees to Record $1.6 Billion Climate Policy Funding Deal
item.description: Turkey and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) on Thursday agreed on a $1.6-billion climate financing package to support Turkey’s climate goals in the biggest climate-focused deal of the Asian bank to date. The deal was announced in Antalya, where Turkey is hosting the COP31 global climate summit until November 20. Under the agreement, AIIB founding member Turkey will access a Climate-Focused Policy-Based Financing (CPBF) loan for the Türkiye Climate Action Acceleration Program (TCAAP) with supplemental…

item.title: Nigeria Hits OPEC Oil Production Quota for Sixth Straight Month
item.description: Nigeria’s crude oil output averaged 1.51 million barrels per day (bpd) in October as OPEC’s biggest African producer pumped to its quota for the sixth consecutive month, data from the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) showed this week. Nigeria last month pumped a total of 1.688 million barrels of crude oil and condensate per day, according to the data from its upstream regulator. item.title: India Boosts Gulf Oil Imports as Russian Crude Loses Its Price Advantage
item.description: India has imported higher volumes of crude oil from the Persian Gulf than from Russia so far in November, for the first time since the Iran war broke out and disrupted the normal supply chain through the Strait of Hormuz. So far this month, India is estimated to have imported about 2.1 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil from the Persian Gulf, compared to 1.8 million bpd flows from Russia, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, citing data by Kpler.
